newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers agree 15 pct cut in greenhouse gases.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers agree 15 pct cut in greenhouse gases.

text.p: EU environment ministers agreed to cut the bloc's emissions of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide from fossil fuels by 15 percent of 1990 levels by 2010, Dutch minister Margreet de Boer told reporters late on Sunday.
"We have an agreement on the reduction of 15 percent for Europe as a whole," de Boer said after chairing a meeting of EU environment ministers.

The deal emerged after an informal session of talks on Sunday aimed at striking a deal to cut EU countries' collective emissions of greenhouse gases, a meeting diplomats had earlier played down as unlikely to produce any result.

Ministers agreed on how to share out individual cuts between countries for only 10 percentage points of the 15 percent pledged, an indication of the difficulties the European Union still faces with its announced target.

De Boer described the 15 percent figure as a firm commitment for the EU to take to international climate change talks in Kyoto, Japan in December. "We go to Kyoto with 15 percent and if that's agreed then we will negotiate about how to share out the remaining 5 percent within the EU," she said.

The Dutch, as holders of the EU presidency, unusually scheduled the meeting on a Sunday in anticipation of two-day, formal ministerial talks on Monday and international talks by climate negotiators starting on Monday in Bonn.
